metadata.title: An elementary counterexample to Long's clique equality
metadata.description:
The full ring of integers of Q(sqrt(10)) gives a complete elementary negative answer to the equality printed in Long Question 7.2 (arXiv:1512.04620v1), using its prime-element convention and without a PID assumption. Both the unit-difference and unit-or-prime-element-difference graphs have clique number two, and the least norm of a nonzero prime ideal is two. The displayed proposed equality therefore compares two with four.

This is a credited elementary exposition, with no claim of novelty, firstness, current worldwide openness, or independent discovery lineage. Lenstra's 1977 Proposition 2.2 already supplies the ideal-residue unit-clique bound. Dummit's 2021 notes explicitly contain the same classical ideal and norm obstruction. Long and Thistlethwaite supply the prime-clique framework; Lopez's 2018 thesis defines the same first prime graph and related higher prime-ideal-power graphs. Combining old ingredients here is not backdated as an earlier printed resolution. The exact historical priority of the full graph conclusion remains unestablished after the scoped audit.

The prime-element convention means a nonzero nonunit generating a prime ideal. It does not mean irreducible element and does not impose the additional Lenstra-Hurwitz unit-surjectivity condition. Higher prime-ideal-power graphs are different for powers at least two. The note computes the quantities in the printed question directly, independently of the journal theorem whose displayed minimum is over principal ideals.

The supporting archive retains the manuscript, immutable original submission, explicit current adjudications, authored mathematical and priority reviews, source-read receipts, and scoped reproducible finite checks. Omitted third-party bodies and the original raw search excerpt ledger are not claimed as portable members. AI tools were used extensively in solving, reconstruction, source review, verification, drafting, and independent internal AI adversarial review. This work is unrefereed; no external human peer review, formal proof-assistant certification, or journal acceptance is claimed. Finite checks are diagnostics rather than a substitute for the written proof.
